elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates" — express defence duty running to Company and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (1): "an allegation that the Site or the Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — the Site is the deliverable under Section 1.1, so scope matches.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (3): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content or user information caused by HDI".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (4): "HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The Company shall give HDI prompt written notice of any such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the Company shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "The Company shall indemnify HDI against third-party claims to the extent arising out of Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law" — no broader Customer indemnity added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (1) covers third-party allegations that the Site or Services infringe or misappropriate IP rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no modification carve-out is included, which is more favourable to Customer, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination carve-out inserted — absence favours Customer, condition inapplicable.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification carve-out inserted — absence favours Customer, condition inapplicable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder for infringing Site or Services.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears anywhere in the inserted language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability cap or super-cap of 3× annual fees is stated in the insertion (and none is needed at the preferred level).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are present in operative language (defence duty for Company and affiliates, four indemnity limbs including IP infringement, notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a narrow reciprocal Company indemnity limited to Content and breach of law).
Fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3× super-cap), which is acceptable because the redline sits at the preferred level rather than the fallback.

Minimal: a single concise insertion of the missing clause; no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages theories, or unrelated boilerplate was added, and existing Section 9(a)/(b) language (including the favourable Globix carve-out) is retained untouched.
Intent preserved: no renumbering, no cross-reference disturbed, and no retained sentence contradicted; the paragraph sits at the end of Section 9 before Section 10.
Repair nit (not a level defect): the inserted paragraph carries no subsection designator — label it "(c) Indemnification." to match the (a)/(b) structure of Section 9.

Verify definitional support before sending: the insertion uses capitalised "Services" and "Content", neither of which is among the resolved definitions (only "Site", "HDI", "Company", "Deerskin Products" are confirmed). If those terms are not defined in the Agreement, replace with "the Site or the services provided by HDI hereunder" and "Company content or user information" to avoid an undefined term.
